newsitem.title: USA: IRS/Treasury guidance on "yield burning" delayed.
newsitem.headline: IRS/Treasury guidance on "yield burning" delayed.

text.p: The IRS told municipal bond groups on Friday that it cannot respond to their concerns about the federal government's recent ruling on "yield burning" until next week, a representative of the groups said.
"They need another week," Amy Dunbar, director of governmental affairs for the National Association of Bond Lawyers, said in a telephone interview.
"They are working on it," said Dunbar, who spoke to an agency official today. "They will tell us something next week."
NABL is one of four industry groups that met August 29 with Internal Revenue Service and U.S. Treasury Dept. officials about the agencies' July 19 enforcement policy on "yield burning."
The policy says issuers of advance refunding bonds can head off possibly having the interest on their bonds declared taxable by entering into "closing agreements" with IRS.

Under such agreements, localities would agree to pay Treasury the difference between the price they paid and the spot price of the securities on the purchase date, plus interest, the IRS' "revenue procedure" says.
Dunbar and others who attended last week's meeting said they left the session with the impression that a response would be issued this week.
